_comment: Two findings about YouTube that fell out of the research rather than being looked for, captured deliberately from batch 34 on the owner's instruction. NOT yet surfaced to visitors — the data exists in a usable shape and the decision about whether to publish it comes at the end of Phase 2. The reason it may be worth publishing: someone searching "learn iOS" finds Sean Allen and has no way to discover that his teaching moved behind a paywall years ago and the channel is now a news show. That gap between what a name is known for and what the channel currently is, is precisely what a search engine cannot tell them and a read catalogue can.

_schema.drift: A creator whose CURRENT catalogue no longer matches what their reputation is for. Each entry: handle, name, knownFor, catalogueNow, scan (what the keyword scan actually returned — the number is the point), categoriesAffected, outcome (rejected | listed-with-caveat), checkedAt.
_schema.collisions: A handle that resolves to a real channel that is not the person or subject sought. Each entry: handle, resolvedTo, sought, note, checkedAt. Two kinds worth distinguishing: a PERSON-name collision, which identityMatch can catch because a name is specific; and a CATEGORY-term collision, which it cannot, because category words are generic enough for any channel to carry them innocently.

drift.name: Sean Allen
drift.knownFor: Swift and SwiftUI teaching; one of the best-known iOS development educators on the platform.
drift.catalogueNow: A weekly iOS news roundup. The teaching moved into paid courses, which the channel description links to.
drift.scan: 300 uploads scanned for swiftui, swift, tutorial, build, how to, beginner, concurrency. 107 long-form hits — and every one is the same roundup format, titled "X, Y, Z & More".

drift.name: Theo (t3.gg)
drift.knownFor: Web frontend and TypeScript education; creator of the T3 stack.
drift.catalogueNow: AI model commentary and reaction — 'NVIDIA Just Lost Their Lead', 'Which AI Models Are Worth Using'.
drift.scan: 50 recent uploads, 30 over twenty minutes, and the long-form list contains no frontend teaching.

drift.name: Jeff Su
drift.knownFor: Workplace and career skills — the channel people recommend for professional communication.
drift.scan: 300 uploads scanned for career, promotion, manager, workplace, politics, feedback, meeting, email, resume. ONE long-form hit, a resume video, in a category that already had creators.

drift.name: Vanessa Lau
drift.knownFor: Social media growth and content strategy teaching.
drift.catalogueNow: Founder vlogs and travel diaries. She states the pivot herself in the channel description.
drift.scan: 588 uploads, 42 of the 50 most recent under two minutes; the long-form is diaries and vlogging-gear reviews.

drift.name: Dr. Todd Grande
drift.knownFor: Credentialed counsellor education — a plausible critic of pop relationship psychology.
drift.catalogueNow: True-crime case commentary with tabloid-style titles.
drift.scan: 4,102 uploads; the 50 most recent are true-crime analyses, median 15 minutes.

drift.name: Code Monkey
drift.knownFor: Unity and C# game development tutorials from a professional indie developer.
drift.catalogueNow: Unity Asset Store roundups and Steam-marketing interviews; teaching largely moved to paid courses.
drift.scan: 250 uploads scanned; 19 long-form hits, most of them asset roundups. Median upload length two minutes.

drift.name: MyWifeQuitHerJob (Steve Chou)
drift.knownFor: Ecommerce operations — sourcing, margins, running a physical-product business.
drift.catalogueNow: Opportunity listicles: '8 Claude AI Side Hustles That Each Make $100K/Yr', '9 UNSEXY Products Quietly Making $10M+'.
drift.scan: 1,247 uploads, median 2 minutes; the long-form is trend-chasing rather than operational teaching.

drift.name: Adam Ragusea
drift.knownFor: Cooking technique explained from first principles — the salt-in-pasta-water genre.
drift.catalogueNow: Substantially food journalism and policy: peanut allergies, farm economics, processed-food regulation, plus an unrelated podcast strand.
drift.scan: 600 uploads scanned to find the technique videos; the fundamentals material is real but older than most of the recent catalogue.

drift.name: Pat Flynn
drift.knownFor: Affiliate marketing done with disclosure; published his own income reports for years.
drift.catalogueNow: Live-streaming setup, short-form video challenges and creator-business content. 29 of the 50 most recent uploads are under two minutes.
drift.scan: 400 uploads scanned for affiliate terms; five long-form hits, four of them the workshops that justify the listing, all well back in the catalogue.

drift.name: The Run Experience
drift.knownFor: Running technique and injury-prevention coaching — 'run better: faster, longer, with fewer injuries', per its own description.
drift.catalogueNow: Race recaps, personal vlogs and challenge videos — a marathon recap, a 30-day cold plunge, a misdiagnosis story.
drift.scan: 300 uploads scanned for form, technique, training, plan, beginner, injury, strength for runners. NINE long-form hits. Dormant since January 2025.

collisions.sought: Chris Voss the FBI hostage negotiator
collisions.note: The trap that produced identityMatch: a channel merely NAMED after a person fails the gate; its own description or recurring upload titles must tie it to them.

collisions.resolvedTo: a military-history animation channel (Pearl Harbor, Midway, Operation Anaconda), 1M-5M subscribers
collisions.note: The trap that produced genericNameCollision(). identityMatch cannot help here: 'operations' is generic enough that any channel in any field carries it innocently.

collisions.resolvedTo: a consulting-careers channel — two long-form videos in 49, both about case interviews
collisions.note: Flagged by the new guard BEFORE it was read, which is the first time the check did the noticing rather than luck.

collisions.resolvedTo: a different Dave Gray — 'Possibilitarian at School of the Possible', a visual-thinking podcast
an unrelated Arabic-language channel with 4,529 uploads
a British creator, not Amy McCready's US organisation
